summary: Meekail Ahmed Nasym, MP for South Galolhu, proposed a resolution asking MPs to state their view on the government's decision to take 14 plots of land away from Malé City Council and make them State property. The Ministry of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development made the decision under the 19th amendment to the Decentralisation Act. The resolution says the council was not consulted and project details were not published, as the law requires, and that the move weakens councils' powers.
keyPoints: Plots listed include Sultan Park, Rasfannu, the fish market and reclaimed area, Carnival, and the council's extension land.
Planned uses named include a pump station, mixed-use commercial buildings, an EV charging facility, a parking building and a conference and exhibition centre.
Cites Article 56-2 of the Decentralisation Act (Law No. 7/2010), which requires consulting the council and publishing project details before land is taken.
Says the plots already earn income in the council's budget that pays for its running costs.
Submitted under Article 189 of Parliament's rules of procedure, dated 20 October 2026.
